questions.text: Aluru Venkata Rao
questions.text_as_printed: Aluru Venkata Rao (Difficult)

answer.value: Aluru Venkata Rao was a great leader who worked for the promotion of Kannada language, culture, and heritage. Seeing the fragmented condition of Karnataka, he lamented: Alas! Where is Karnataka?... Who will unite the Karnataka that has been divided into many parts? Is there anyone with such devotion? His aim was to make Kannadigas aware of the glorious history and heritage of Karnataka. For this purpose, he wrote the book The Glorious Past of Karnataka (Karnatakada Gatavaibhava) and published it at his own expense. The book became a great source of inspiration. In A.D. 1941, the Kannadigas of Hyderabad honoured him with the title "Karnataka Kula Purohita" (High Priest of Karnataka).

questions.text: Fazal Ali Commission
questions.text_as_printed: Fazal Ali Commission (Difficult)

answer.value: The Central Government appointed the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) to recommend the reorganisation of Indian states. Its chairman was S. Fazal Ali, and the other members were H. N. Kunzru and K. M. Panikkar. The Commission submitted its report in A.D. 1955. Based on its recommendations, the states of India were reorganised mainly on the basis of language and administrative convenience. Although most political parties accepted the Commission's report, Kannadigas strongly protested against the recommendation to include Kasaragod in Kerala and the recommendations concerning Bellary district. The Mysore Legislative Assembly resolved that Bellary should not be separated from Mysore and that the new state should be named Mysore State.
